name: Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 7:00 PM Morristown High School Media Center The first Coffee with the Superintendent for the 2026–2027 school year was held on Thursday, October 15, 2026. The minutes from the meeting are recorded below. The following summary was created using notes generated by Zoom, AI Companion Referendum Implementation Update The Morris Future website has been created to share project timelines, frequently asked questions, and ongoing updates. The previous Referendum site has been archived within this new hub and remains fully accessible. This website will be updated frequently to keep the community informed of the progress. Questions can still be directed to morrisfuture@msdk12.net , which the district will continue to monitor this email regularly. The Construction Schedule page has full details regarding project timelines. Project information is organized by year and by building. Below is an overview of the timeline presented: 2027-2028 - Year 1 (Start Summer 2027) Roof Replacements: Full roof replacements are scheduled for Alfred Vail, Normandy Park, and Frelinghuysen Middle School (FMS). Completing this work first is essential to ensure each building is fully weather-sealed before interior upgrades can begin. Please note that progress is weather-dependent, as insurance regulations prohibit roofing work when there is a 30% or higher chance of rain. HVAC & Air Conditioning: HVAC conversions and air conditioning repairs in Alfred Vail, Hillcrest, and Normandy Park will begin during the summer of 2027. Due to a 14-month project timeline, active air conditioning is projected to be fully operational by the fall of 2028. Immediate Upgrades: Middle and high school science lab renovations, along with initial bathroom renovations at Thomas Jefferson, Alexander Hamilton, and Frelinghuysen Middle School, will begin Summer 2027. 2028-2029 - Year 2 Projects Classroom Additions (Sussex Avenue & FMS): Construction will begin in the summer of 2028. Work will take place in sealed-off, secure construction zones, with final connections to the main school buildings completed during the final phase to minimize disruption to students. Both additions are scheduled for completion by the start of the 2029–2030 school year. Morristown High School Pool Replacement: The current pool will remain in use for the next two swim seasons. Demolition and construction will begin after the 2028 swim season. During the estimated 18-to-24-month construction period, swim teams will need to utilize alternative facilities. The new pool is projected to open for the 2030 swim season. Auditorium Renovations: Morristown High School Auditorium: Renovation will begin immediately following the Spring 2028 musical. The high school auditorium will close through the summer, with the goal of reopening in time for the Fall 2028 production (or using the FMS auditorium as a contingency). FMS Auditorium: Work on the FMS auditorium will be staggered and will not begin until the MHS auditorium renovation is complete, ensuring one district venue remains available. 2029-2031 - Years 3-5 The heaviest construction activities will occur during School Years 2 and 3. Years 4 and 5 will focus on remaining window replacements, interior finishes, and final bathroom renovations across district schools. Preliminary results of Spring 2026 Standardized Tests At the November Board of Education meeting, district leadership will deliver a comprehensive presentation of the Spring 2026 standardized testing results across all schools. This detailed review will cover performance data for the New Jersey Student Learning Assessments (NJSLA) and Advanced Placement (AP) exams, as well as ACCESS testing results for bilingual and multilingual learners. Below is a preview of what you can expect to see in that presentation: Overall District Performances: Initial review of the NJSLA Language Arts data shows that over 58% of students across all grade levels met or exceeded grade-level expectations . While overall ELA proficiency saw a slight 2.2% decrease compared to 2025, a higher proportion of students achieved the highest performance tier ("Exceeding Expectations") than in prior years. District mathematics proficiency , which combines both Level 4 (Meeting Expectations) and Level 5 (Exceeding Expectations), increased to 38% in 2026, up from 33.8% in 2025 for an overall gain of 4.2 percentage points. Additionally, the proportion of students achieving Level 5 reached a record 15.7%. District science proficiency , which combines both the Proficient and Advanced Proficient categories, held steady at 28.8% across tested grades 5, 8, and 11, aligning closely with historical performance trends. Frelinghuysen Middle School (Grade 6-8): Middle school math performance saw substantial gains across the board following last year’s schedule restructuring, which expanded math instruction to every day alongside the adoption of a new curriculum and enhanced instructional models. Grade 7 Math , a key benchmark for secondary academic readiness, proficiency jumped 19.6% year-over-year from 2025, contributing to a two-year passing rate increase of 33.8% and a 15.7 percentage point increase in students reaching Level 5 (Exceeding Expectations). Grade 8 Math proficiency also rose 15.0% year-over-year. High-level middle school courses delivered outstanding results as well: 79.6% of middle school Algebra I students met or exceeded expectations, with 21.1% achieving Level 5, while students taking Middle School Geometry achieved exceptional performance with 100% reaching proficiency (34.1% Meeting and 65.9% Exceeding Expectations). Morristown High School (Grade 9–12): Grade 9 ELA proficiency reached 60.2% (38.8% Meeting and 21.4% Exceeding Expectations), outperforming the New Jersey state average of 55.2%. At Morristown High School, Algebra 1 showed steady improvement with proficiency increasing by 2.8% year-over-year (12.1% meeting expectations). Meanwhile, Algebra 2 reached a 24.9% proficiency rate (20.9% Meeting and 4.0% Exceeding Expectations), reflecting significant growth driven by targeted support initiatives such as the Algebra 2 Boot Camp, expanded summer programming, and enhanced curricular materials. Additionally, subgroup analysis highlighted positive trends, including a 7% increase in proficiency for students receiving Section 504 services, while district teams remain focused on narrowing achievement gaps for multilingual learners and special education cohorts. Grade 11 Science performance exceeded the state benchmark, with 35.0% of students scoring Proficient or Advanced Proficient compared to the New Jersey average of 32.7%. Academic Programming, Teaching & Learning Increase access to and participation in Advanced Placement courses at Morristown High School by removing barriers such as affordability, while providing consistent support to ensure success for all students. Advanced Placement By the Numbers 2025-2026 • Participation Rate: Increased 15% to 96% participation • Number of Exams Taken: Increased from 783 to 1,124 • Pass Rate: Increased 10% • Total AP Students: Increased from 384 students to 528 (Increase in senior student participation) Ongoing Supports for Advanced Placement • Exam Cost: With the support of the Board of Education, all exam costs are covered by the Morris School District • Summer Program: AP Bootcamp - providing students with a glimpse of an AP course prior to the upcoming school year. Students identified based on course selection and AP Potential Tool • Before/After School Support (AP Collaboration Hub): MHS provide before and after school AP tutoring to interested students as well as Exam Review Sessions Athletic Director Search Update The search process for the new Athletic Director is underway following the receipt of over 100 applications. The goal is to select and fill the position by December. Mr. Mark Manning, Morristown High School Principal, will oversee the Athletic Department in the interim. The search is progressing in three phases: • Phase 1 (Current): Initial broad screening of candidates. • Phase 2: Committee interviews involving coaches and staff members. • Phase 3: Final interviews involving parent volunteers. Additionally, an Athletic Director Survey was launched with an overwhelming response rate, and the committee expressed appreciation for the valuable community and parent feedback. District Events, Announcements, and Community Input Opportunities Screenagers Screening (Digital Citizenship Week) On Thursday, October 22 at 6:00 PM , the Morris School District, in partnership with TEAM, will host a live screening of Screenagers: Elementary School Edition in the Morristown High School Auditorium. The event is open to K–8 students and parents to encourage dialogue on helping children thrive in a digital world. The screening aligns with next week’s Digital Citizenship Week , which focuses on teaching students responsible technology use. View the Event Flyer for full details and register to attend this event. MHS Fall Production Tickets are currently on sale for the Morristown High School fall production of Dracula , with performances scheduled for November 20, 21, and 22. Purchase tickets at MHSTIX.com. STEM Academy Applications Applications are open for current 8th-grade students interested in the STEM Academy. The application deadline is November 30 . Complete details are available on the STEM Academy page of the MHS Website. District Social Media Update District social media engagement has increased significantly this school year, offering community members a view into classroom learning and district events. District channels regularly reshare school highlights, including athletics, school spirit events, and upcoming productions. To boost school engagement, the district launched a monthly internal social media challenge. October’s theme is Creativity , with new themed challenges to follow each month. HIB Parent Workshop Recaps In recognition of the Week of Respect, Board Attorney David Rubin facilitated a parent workshop providing updates on Harassment, Intimidation, and Bullying (HIB) law. A recording of the session is available on the HIB page of the district website for those who could not attend. Community Input Opportunities • Wellness Survey - A Wellness Survey was distributed in September to gather feedback from parents and guardians. The survey remains open, and parent participation is strongly encouraged, as the results will guide future events and parent workshops. This survey will remain open for another week. • Strategic Plan Survey - Community input is requested regarding the strategic plan implemented in the fall of 2024. This survey will remain open through November 15 . Morris School District Mission Statement It is the mission of the Morris School District to empower each student to ascend academically, socially, and emotionally by providing equal access to continuous opportunities for achieving academic excellence, developing meaningful relationships, and becoming future ready.

Preliminary results of Spring 2026 Standardized Tests At the November Board of Education meeting, district leadership will deliver a comprehensive presentation of the Spring 2026 standardized testing results across all schools. This detailed review will cover performance data for the New Jersey Student Learning Assessments (NJSLA) and Advanced Placement (AP) exams, as well as ACCESS testing results for bilingual and multilingual learners. Below is a preview of what you can expect to see in that presentation: Overall District Performances: Initial review of the NJSLA Language Arts data shows that over 58% of students across all grade levels met or exceeded grade-level expectations . While overall ELA proficiency saw a slight 2.2% decrease compared to 2025, a higher proportion of students achieved the highest performance tier ("Exceeding Expectations") than in prior years. District mathematics proficiency , which combines both Level 4 (Meeting Expectations) and Level 5 (Exceeding Expectations), increased to 38% in 2026, up from 33.8% in 2025 for an overall gain of 4.2 percentage points. Additionally, the proportion of students achieving Level 5 reached a record 15.7%. District science proficiency , which combines both the Proficient and Advanced Proficient categories, held steady at 28.8% across tested grades 5, 8, and 11, aligning closely with historical performance trends. Frelinghuysen Middle School (Grade 6-8): Middle school math performance saw substantial gains across the board following last year’s schedule restructuring, which expanded math instruction to every day alongside the adoption of a new curriculum and enhanced instructional models. Grade 7 Math , a key benchmark for secondary academic readiness, proficiency jumped 19.6% year-over-year from 2025, contributing to a two-year passing rate increase of 33.8% and a 15.7 percentage point increase in students reaching Level 5 (Exceeding Expectations). Grade 8 Math proficiency also rose 15.0% year-over-year. High-level middle school courses delivered outstanding results as well: 79.6% of middle school Algebra I students met or exceeded expectations, with 21.1% achieving Level 5, while students taking Middle School Geometry achieved exceptional performance with 100% reaching proficiency (34.1% Meeting and 65.9% Exceeding Expectations). Morristown High School (Grade 9–12): Grade 9 ELA proficiency reached 60.2% (38.8% Meeting and 21.4% Exceeding Expectations), outperforming the New Jersey state average of 55.2%. At Morristown High School, Algebra 1 showed steady improvement with proficiency increasing by 2.8% year-over-year (12.1% meeting expectations). Meanwhile, Algebra 2 reached a 24.9% proficiency rate (20.9% Meeting and 4.0% Exceeding Expectations), reflecting significant growth driven by targeted support initiatives such as the Algebra 2 Boot Camp, expanded summer programming, and enhanced curricular materials. Additionally, subgroup analysis highlighted positive trends, including a 7% increase in proficiency for students receiving Section 504 services, while district teams remain focused on narrowing achievement gaps for multilingual learners and special education cohorts. Grade 11 Science performance exceeded the state benchmark, with 35.0% of students scoring Proficient or Advanced Proficient compared to the New Jersey average of 32.7%. name: As part of our commitment to maintaining a safe environment for all students, staff, and visitors, we want to remind families of our district policy regarding motorized vehicles (including e-bikes, e-scooters, and hoverboards). Student Operation: Students are strictly prohibited from operating motorized vehicles on school grounds. Please note that state and local regulations also govern or restrict underage/unlicensed operation across Rahway, Union County, and New Jersey. Unauthorized Devices on Campus: If a student brings an unauthorized motorized device onto school property, it will be held safely in the main office. Administration will contact parents/guardians daily until the device is retrieved by an adult. Please review the attached documents. If you have any questions or need further clarification, please contact your school's main office directly. Thank you for your continued partnership in keeping our school community safe.

name: As Rahway Public Schools honors Hispanic Heritage Month, students across all grade levels engage in dynamic activities recognizing the history, cultures, and contributions of Hispanic and Latino communities. From elementary read-alouds and student-created art displays to interactive music performances, culinary explorations, and historical research projects at Rahway Middle School and Rahway High School, the district’s schools bring cultural traditions to life in the classroom. These educational observances foster cultural pride, promote inclusivity, and connect classroom learning with the broader heritage celebrations happening throughout the Rahway community. To stay informed about specific celebrations, families should expect customized news and schedules sent directly from their child’s individual school building. Because events—such as guest presentations, spirit days, evening showcases, and family workshops—vary by building, principals and staff share details through district email blasts, text alerts, school newsletters, our website, and social media. Get ready to join the festivities, honor these rich cultural traditions, and celebrate the extraordinary spirit of our students and community all month long!

name: As we celebrate Custodian Appreciation Week, I want to extend our heartfelt thanks to the incredible custodial and facilities staff who keep our schools running smoothly each and every day. Behind every clean hallway, bright classroom, and well-maintained facility is a team of hardworking professionals who take immense pride in their work. Their effort behind the scenes ensures our schools remain safe, healthy, and inviting spaces where our students can focus on learning and thriving. Our custodians do so much more than keep our buildings spotless—they are an integral part of our school culture, greeting students with warm smiles, helping out whenever needed, and showing what true dedication looks like. On behalf of the entire administration, board of education, and school community, thank you to our custodial team for your relentless hard work and commitment to the Rahway Public Schools family. Please take a moment this week to share your appreciation with our custodians when you see them across the district!

name: As we celebrate National Principals Month, I want to take this opportunity to extend our deepest gratitude to the visionary leaders who guide, inspire, and support our school communities every single day. The role of a principal is vast and deeply impactful—they are the heart of our buildings, balancing administrative duties with the invaluable work of fostering safe, nurturing, and rigorous learning environments. Their dedication ensures that our educators are supported, our families are engaged, and, most importantly, our students are empowered to reach their fullest potential. We are incredibly fortunate in Rahway to have such an exceptional and passionate group of leaders at the helm of our schools. Please join me in celebrating and thanking our outstanding principals who champion the #RahwayRocks spirit daily: Dr. Michelle Panichi at Rahway High School, Ms. Isabel Colon at the Rahway 7th & 8th Grade Academy, Dr. Patrick Holness at Franklin Elementary School, Dr. Joseph Cordero at Grover Cleveland Elementary School, Ms. Dee Jones at Madison Elementary School, and Dr. Leslie Septor at Roosevelt Elementary School. Their unwavering commitment to academic excellence, inclusivity, and leadership shapes the bright futures of our students and the strength of our entire district. Thank you, Rahway principals, for all that you do!

name: Athletics Department Season Update Today is a big day for our senior girls on the soccer team! The squad will be playing at home against Carteret at the Madison Ave field. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:00 PM, so be sure to come out and support the team as they continue to grow and compete. Get ready for an exciting and emotional night on the gridiron, as our stellar 7-1 football team takes on Edison at 7:00 PM at Madden Field! This is a pivotal matchup, serving as the final game before the state tournament playoffs officially begin next week. Most importantly, it is Senior Night for our football, cheerleading, and marching band members! Come pack the stands to honor these dedicated seniors, cheer on the boys, and enjoy the fantastic halftime performances. The high school boys soccer team has officially wrapped up their regular season with a very solid 10-7 record. Though the team recently suffered a heartbreaking last-second defeat in the county quarterfinals, they are quickly regrouping and getting ready to make a run in the state playoffs starting in November. On the court, our girls volleyball team has battled to an 11-10 record this season. The girls recently faced a tough elimination loss to Summit in the county tournament, capping off a competitive stretch of matches against tough opponents including Summit, Oak Knoll, Roselle Park, and Linden. With a junior-heavy roster this year, the team is packed with potential and is poised for a very strong season next fall. A huge congratulations goes out to the girls tennis team for a fantastic season! The team's hard work paid off, as they proudly secured an impressive 3rd place finish in the highly competitive Valley division. Our boys and girls cross country teams are rebuilding this season and have been competing hard in a tough division. We look forward to watching these athletes grow over the next several seasons. We are thrilled to celebrate a historic milestone for our athletics department indoors: the inaugural season of our Freshmen and Middle School volleyball teams! This is the first time ever that we have offered these programs, and we are incredibly excited to watch these young athletes develop their skills and build a foundation for the future of our high school team. Out on the pitch, we are seeing fantastic things from our middle school boys and girls soccer programs! These teams serve as an incredibly strong feeder program for our high school squads and have generated a tremendous amount of interest school-wide. With so much young talent and enthusiasm, the future of our high school soccer programs looks exceptionally bright!

name: Dear Rahway Community, As October unfolds across Rahway Public Schools, the 2026–2027 school year continues to build wonderful momentum. This month brings meaningful opportunities to honor our dedicated leaders, celebrate our rich diversity, unite for important causes, and share a deeper look into the learning taking place in our classrooms. First, we are proud to recognize National Principals Month! Our school principals are the heart of our buildings, providing visionary leadership, unwavering support, and dedication to our students, teachers, and staff every single day. Their tireless efforts behind the scenes and in the halls shape positive school cultures where everyone can thrive, and we extend our deepest gratitude for everything they do to guide our schools forward. As October progresses, we are also excited to continue our district-wide celebration of Hispanic Heritage Month. Our classrooms and hallways remain filled with engaging activities, creative projects, and inspiring lessons that honor the rich histories, vibrant traditions, and lasting contributions of Hispanic and Latino cultures within our community and beyond. In addition, our district stands united in observing Breast Cancer Awareness Month throughout October. Together, our Rahway family joins in raising awareness, honoring courageous survivors, remembering those we have lost, and supporting ongoing efforts to find a cure. Finally, we are thrilled to include special features directly from our Curriculum & Instruction Department. These updates will offer families an inside look at the innovative academic programs, key learning initiatives, and instructional strategies being implemented to ensure every child achieves their full potential. Each of these celebrations and updates reminds us of the strength found in our theme, “Elevate Together.” Thank you for your ongoing partnership, care, and enthusiasm as we work as one community to support our students every step of the way. Wishing our entire Rahway community a wonderful and inspiring week ahead as we continue to Elevate Together! Warm regards, Dr. Aleya Shoieb Superintendent of Schools

This annual tradition gives our entire community the opportunity to recognize the extraordinary teachers and educational services professionals who go above and beyond for our students every day. Wishing our entire Rahway community a wonderful and productive week ahead as we continue to Elevate Together! Warm regards, Dr. Aleya Shoieb Superintendent of Schools

name: Diagnostic Testing Begins Throughout Rahway Public Schools Diagnostic testing is underway across the Rahway school district to help launch a successful academic year. Students in kindergarten through 8th grade are taking i-Ready assessments, while high school students are taking STAR Renaissance tests. These digital assessments adjust to each student's skill level in reading and math, giving teachers a quick, clear look at what students already understand and where they might need extra support. The results from these early tests create an initial data point for every student—much like a snapshot of their current skills at the start of the year. Think of this score as a starting line rather than a final grade. It gives teachers a clear benchmark to build on, making it simple to track individual progress and measure academic growth as the months go on. Teachers will analyze and extrapolate this assessment data to guide their instruction for the remainder of the school year. By using these insights to shape daily lessons, teachers can group students by learning needs, offer targeted help on tricky concepts, and provide extra challenges for students who are ready to move ahead. This ensures that classroom learning is personalized to help every Rahway student succeed.

name: October Curriculum & Instruction Focus 🍂 Helping Students Think, Talk & Grow Learning is about more than getting the right answer. This month, we are encouraging students to think deeply, explain their ideas, work through challenges, ask questions, and take greater ownership of their learning. Families can support this work at home by asking questions that encourage children to think rather than simply answer. 📚 K–6 | Think It. Explain It. Show It. What’s Happening in Learning? Across our elementary classrooms, students are being encouraged to become active participants in their learning. In mathematics, teachers are creating opportunities for students to explain why and how they know, engage in mathematical conversations, and experience productive struggle while solving problems. These same habits of thinking can be encouraged across reading, writing, science, and social studies. 🎓 7–12 | Own Your Learning What’s Happening in Learning? As our middle and high school students continue through the year, we want them to become increasingly aware of what they are learning, how they are learning it, and how they know when they have been successful. This connects directly to the district's instructional focus on student ownership. 🌎 Supporting Our Multilingual Learners Parent-teacher conferences are an opportunity to learn about your child’s progress and work together with their teacher. Your questions and insights are an important part of your child’s success. It is okay to ask questions, request clarification, or ask for an interpreter. Your home language is an asset. Use the questions below to guide the conversation with your child’s teacher and identify ways you can support your child’s learning at home. How is my child doing academically in your class? What are my child’s strengths? What are they doing especially well? What areas does my child need more support with? How is my child’s English developing in speaking, listening, reading, and writing? Does my child participate in class and feel comfortable asking questions or asking for help? How does my child interact with classmates? Do they seem to feel comfortable and included? What supports or strategies are you using to help my child understand the lessons while they are learning English? Is my child completing assignments and homework? Are there any assignments or skills we should focus on? What can we do at home—in English or in our home language—to support what my child is learning? What is one goal we can work on together before the next report card or conference? Meet the Bilingual and ESL Team! Stay Connected with Us! Keep an eye on your mailbox each month for El Rincón Familiar , our ESL/Bilingual Department newsletter! Discover helpful resources, important updates, upcoming events, and practical tips to support your child’s learning at home. We look forward to staying connected with you and your family! ❤️ Healthy Habits at Home Healthy Bodies. Ready Minds. Students are learning that healthy habits can help their bodies and minds be ready to learn. Elementary students are engaging in movement, healthy-habit discussions, mindful breathing, brain breaks, and opportunities for reflection throughout the school day. 🏠 October Family Learning Tip ⭐ October Family Challenge The Masterpiece Exchange: Art Meets Literature Rahway Public Schools and the Rahway Public Library are proud to present The Masterpiece Exchange: Works of Art for Works of Literature! This district-wide partnership showcases student visual artwork at the public library each month, connecting visual storytelling directly with ELA learning. Program Highlights: Monthly Student Exhibitions: Student artwork from across our schools is featured in rotating monthly displays at the Rahway Public Library. Library Field Trips: 2nd and 5th-grade students visit the library to view their peers' art, explore literary resources, and sign up for public library cards. Cross-Curricular Learning: Connects visual art concepts with ELA reading comprehension, critical analysis, and creative expression aligned with New Jersey Student Learning Standards. 🗓️ 2026–2027 Exhibition Highlights Sept & Oct: Rahway Academy ( Community & Breast Cancer Awareness ) Nov & Dec: Roosevelt & Franklin ( Fall/Native American Heritage & Winter Traditions ) Jan & Feb: Rahway High School ( Windows of Understanding / MLK Day ) March–May: Cleveland & Madison ( National Reading Month, Environmental Themes, & Cultural Perspectives ) June: District Staff Showcase Be sure to stop by the Rahway Public Library this month to view the incredible creative talents of our Rahway students!

name: Rahway Public Schools Celebrates Hispanic Heritage Month As Rahway Public Schools honors Hispanic Heritage Month, students across all grade levels engage in dynamic activities recognizing the history, cultures, and contributions of Hispanic and Latino communities. From elementary read-alouds and student-created art displays to interactive music performances, culinary explorations, and historical research projects at Rahway Middle School and Rahway High School, the district’s schools bring cultural traditions to life in the classroom. These educational observances foster cultural pride, promote inclusivity, and connect classroom learning with the broader heritage celebrations happening throughout the Rahway community. To stay informed about specific celebrations, families should expect customized news and schedules sent directly from their child’s individual school building. Because events—such as guest presentations, spirit days, evening showcases, and family workshops—vary by building, principals and staff share details through district email blasts, text alerts, school newsletters, our website, and social media. Get ready to join the festivities, honor these rich cultural traditions, and celebrate the extraordinary spirit of our students and community all month long!

name: Rahway Public Schools Honors Our Principals As we celebrate National Principals Month, I want to take this opportunity to extend our deepest gratitude to the visionary leaders who guide, inspire, and support our school communities every single day. The role of a principal is vast and deeply impactful—they are the heart of our buildings, balancing administrative duties with the invaluable work of fostering safe, nurturing, and rigorous learning environments. Their dedication ensures that our educators are supported, our families are engaged, and, most importantly, our students are empowered to reach their fullest potential. We are incredibly fortunate in Rahway to have such an exceptional and passionate group of leaders at the helm of our schools. Please join me in celebrating and thanking our outstanding principals who champion the #RahwayRocks spirit daily: Dr. Michelle Panichi at Rahway High School, Ms. Isabel Colon at the Rahway 7th & 8th Grade Academy, Dr. Patrick Holness at Franklin Elementary School, Dr. Joseph Cordero at Grover Cleveland Elementary School, Ms. Dee Jones at Madison Elementary School, and Dr. Leslie Septor at Roosevelt Elementary School. Their unwavering commitment to academic excellence, inclusivity, and leadership shapes the bright futures of our students and the strength of our entire district. Thank you, Rahway principals, for all that you do!

name: The Masterpiece Exchange: Art Meets Literature Rahway Public Schools and the Rahway Public Library are proud to present The Masterpiece Exchange: Works of Art for Works of Literature! This district-wide partnership showcases student visual artwork at the public library each month, connecting visual storytelling directly with ELA learning. Program Highlights: Monthly Student Exhibitions: Student artwork from across our schools is featured in rotating monthly displays at the Rahway Public Library. Library Field Trips: 2nd and 5th-grade students visit the library to view their peers' art, explore literary resources, and sign up for public library cards. Cross-Curricular Learning: Connects visual art concepts with ELA reading comprehension, critical analysis, and creative expression aligned with New Jersey Student Learning Standards. 🗓️ 2026–2027 Exhibition Highlights Sept & Oct: Rahway Academy ( Community & Breast Cancer Awareness ) Nov & Dec: Roosevelt & Franklin ( Fall/Native American Heritage & Winter Traditions ) Jan & Feb: Rahway High School ( Windows of Understanding / MLK Day ) March–May: Cleveland & Madison ( National Reading Month, Environmental Themes, & Cultural Perspectives ) June: District Staff Showcase Be sure to stop by the Rahway Public Library this month to view the incredible creative talents of our Rahway students!

Program Highlights: Monthly Student Exhibitions: Student artwork from across our schools is featured in rotating monthly displays at the Rahway Public Library. Library Field Trips: 2nd and 5th-grade students visit the library to view their peers' art, explore literary resources, and sign up for public library cards. Cross-Curricular Learning: Connects visual art concepts with ELA reading comprehension, critical analysis, and creative expression aligned with New Jersey Student Learning Standards. 🗓️ 2026–2027 Exhibition Highlights Sept & Oct: Rahway Academy ( Community & Breast Cancer Awareness ) Nov & Dec: Roosevelt & Franklin ( Fall/Native American Heritage & Winter Traditions ) Jan & Feb: Rahway High School ( Windows of Understanding / MLK Day ) March–May: Cleveland & Madison ( National Reading Month, Environmental Themes, & Cultural Perspectives ) June: District Staff Showcase Be sure to stop by the Rahway Public Library this month to view the incredible creative talents of our Rahway students!

name: This week, October 19–23, our school community celebrated National School Bus Safety Week 2026. Throughout the week, the New Jersey Department of Education (NJDOE) shared safety campaign highlights across their social channels, and we encourage families to visit their pages to like and share those valuable reminders. Bus safety remains an ongoing community effort where everyone can be a hero, because student safety starts with all of us. With sincere appreciation for our transportation team, thank you for your partnership.

Your involvement will help celebrate the outstanding educators who make a difference in our children's lives every day.

name: We are thrilled to announce that we will be honoring our outstanding students who achieved the highest scores on the New Jersey Student Learning Assessments (NJSLA) at the upcoming Board of Education meeting on Tuesday, October 27. Reaching the top tier of performance on these state assessments reflects remarkable academic discipline, curiosity, and persistent effort throughout the school year. This milestone is a proud reflection not only of our honorees' dedication, but also of the tireless guidance of our educators and the steady encouragement of their families. We look forward to shining a well-deserved spotlight on these scholars and commemorating the high standard of excellence they have set for our entire district. We warmly invite our entire community; families, neighbors, educators, and local supporters to come out and pack the room to celebrate these extraordinary young leaders. Academic milestones of this caliber deserve to be shared by the entire community, and having a full house to applaud their accomplishments makes this recognition unforgettable for our students. Please mark your calendars for Tuesday, October 27, and join us in the audience to cheer on these scholars, honor their hard work, and show them how proud we are of their achievements.

name: 🌎 Supporting Our Multilingual Learners Parent-teacher conferences are an opportunity to learn about your child’s progress and work together with their teacher. Your questions and insights are an important part of your child’s success. It is okay to ask questions, request clarification, or ask for an interpreter. Your home language is an asset. Use the questions below to guide the conversation with your child’s teacher and identify ways you can support your child’s learning at home. How is my child doing academically in your class? What are my child’s strengths? What are they doing especially well? What areas does my child need more support with? How is my child’s English developing in speaking, listening, reading, and writing? Does my child participate in class and feel comfortable asking questions or asking for help? How does my child interact with classmates? Do they seem to feel comfortable and included? What supports or strategies are you using to help my child understand the lessons while they are learning English? Is my child completing assignments and homework? Are there any assignments or skills we should focus on? What can we do at home—in English or in our home language—to support what my child is learning? What is one goal we can work on together before the next report card or conference?

name: 🍂 Helping Students Think, Talk & Grow Learning is about more than getting the right answer. This month, we are encouraging students to think deeply, explain their ideas, work through challenges, ask questions, and take greater ownership of their learning. Families can support this work at home by asking questions that encourage children to think rather than simply answer. 📚 K–6 | Think It. Explain It. Show It. What’s Happening in Learning? Across our elementary classrooms, students are being encouraged to become active participants in their learning. In mathematics, teachers are creating opportunities for students to explain why and how they know, engage in mathematical conversations, and experience productive struggle while solving problems. These same habits of thinking can be encouraged across reading, writing, science, and social studies.
